pli-tv-kd1:1.0.1: 1. The Story about the Awakening (Tree) (Conditional Origination)
pli-tv-kd1:1.1.1: At that time the Awakened One, the Fortunate One, was dwelling near Uruvelā, on the bank of the river Nerañjarā, at the root of the Awakening tree, in the first (period) after the complete and perfect Awakening.
pli-tv-kd1:1.1.2: o Then at that time the Fortunate One sat at the root of the Awakening tree in one cross-legged posture for seven days experiencing the happiness of liberation.
pli-tv-kd1:1.2.1: Then the Fortunate One, for the first watch of the night, applied his mind thoroughly to conditional origination in forward and reverse order:
pli-tv-kd1:1.2.2: “Because of ignorance there are (volitional) processes, because of (volitional) processes: consciousness, because of consciousness: mind and body, because of mind and body: the six sense spheres, because of the six sense spheres: contact, because of contact: feeling, because of feeling: craving, because of craving: attachment, because of attachment: continuation, because of continuation: birth, because of birth: old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) arise,
pli-tv-kd1:1.2.3: and so there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering.
pli-tv-kd1:1.2.4: But from the complete fading away and cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of (volitional) processes, from the cessation of (volitional) processes, the cessation of consciousness, from the cessation of consciousness, the cessation of mind and body, from the cessation of mind and body, the cessation of the six sense spheres, from the cessation of the six sense spheres, the cessation of contact, from the cessation of contact, the cessation of feeling, from the cessation of feeling, the cessation of craving, from the cessation of craving, the cessation of attachment, from the cessation of attachment, the cessation of continuation, from the cessation of continuation, the cessation of birth, from the cessation of birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) cease,
pli-tv-kd1:1.2.5: and so there is a cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:1.3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:1.3.2: “When (the nature of) things becomes really manifest
pli-tv-kd1:1.3.5: Since he knows (the nature of a) thing and its cause.”
pli-tv-kd1:1.4.1: Then the Fortunate One, for the middle watch of the night, applied his mind thoroughly to conditional origination in forward and reverse order:
pli-tv-kd1:1.4.2: “Because of ignorance there are (volitional) processes, because of (volitional) processes: consciousness, because of consciousness: mind and body, because of mind and body: the six sense spheres, because of the six sense spheres: contact, because of contact: feeling, because of feeling: craving, because of craving: attachment, because of attachment: continuation, because of continuation: birth, because of birth: old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) arise,
pli-tv-kd1:1.4.3: and so there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering. But from the complete fading away and cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of (volitional) processes, from the cessation of (volitional) processes, the cessation of consciousness, from the cessation of consciousness, the cessation of mind and body, from the cessation of mind and body, the cessation of the six sense spheres, from the cessation of the six sense spheres, the cessation of contact, from the cessation of contact, the cessation of feeling, from the cessation of feeling, the cessation of craving, from the cessation of craving, the cessation of attachment, from the cessation of attachment, the cessation of continuation,
pli-tv-kd1:1.4.4: from the cessation of continuation, the cessation of birth, from the cessation of birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) cease, and so there is a cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:1.5.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:1.5.2: “When (the nature of) things becomes really manifest
pli-tv-kd1:1.5.5: Since the destruction of causes has been understood.”
pli-tv-kd1:1.6.1: Then the Fortunate One, for the last watch of the night, applied his mind thoroughly to conditional origination in forward and reverse order:
pli-tv-kd1:1.6.2: “Because of ignorance there are (volitional) processes, because of (volitional) processes: consciousness, because of consciousness: mind and body, because of mind and body: the six sense spheres, because of the six sense spheres: contact, because of contact: feeling, because of feeling: craving, because of craving: attachment, because of attachment: continuation, because of continuation: birth, because of birth: old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) arise,
pli-tv-kd1:1.6.3: and so there is an origination of this whole mass of suffering. But from the complete fading away and cessation of ignorance, there is the cessation of (volitional) processes, from the cessation of (volitional) processes, the cessation of consciousness, from the cessation of consciousness, the cessation of mind and body, from the cessation of mind and body, the cessation of the six sense spheres, from the cessation of the six sense spheres, the cessation of contact, from the cessation of contact, the cessation of feeling, from the cessation of feeling, the cessation of craving, from the cessation of craving, the cessation of attachment, from the cessation of attachment, the cessation of continuation,
pli-tv-kd1:1.6.4: from the cessation of continuation, the cessation of birth, from the cessation of birth, old age, death, grief, lamentation, pain, sorrow, and despair (all) cease, and so there is a cessation of this whole mass of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:1.7.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:1.7.2: “When (the nature of) things becomes really manifest
pli-tv-kd1:1.7.5: Just like the sun lighting up the firmament.”
pli-tv-kd1:1.7.6: The Story about the Bodhi (tree) is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:2.1.0: 2. The Story about the Goatherd’s (Tree) (The Grumbling Brāhmaṇa)
pli-tv-kd1:2.1.1: Then with the passing of seven days, the Fortunate One, after arising from that concentration, approached the Goatherd’s Banyan (tree) from the root of the Awakening tree, and after approaching the root of the Goatherds’ Banyan tree he sat in one cross-legged posture for seven days experiencing the happiness of liberation.
pli-tv-kd1:2.2.1: Then a certain brāhmaṇa who was a grumbler by nature approached the Fortunate One,
pli-tv-kd1:2.2.2: and after approaching he exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One,
pli-tv-kd1:2.2.3: and after exchanging courteous talk and greetings, he stood on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:2.2.4: While standing on one side that brāhmaṇa said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:2.2.5: “To what extent, dear Gotama, is one a brāhmaṇa? And again what things make one a brāhmaṇa?”
pli-tv-kd1:2.3.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:2.3.3: Not grumbling, free from blemish, self-restrained,
pli-tv-kd1:2.3.4: With perfect understanding, (and) the spiritual life accomplished,
pli-tv-kd1:2.3.5: Righteously he might speak a word about the Brahman,
pli-tv-kd1:2.3.6: For him there is no arrogance anywhere in the world.”
pli-tv-kd1:2.3.7: The Story about the Goatherd’s (Tree) is finished
pli-tv-kd1:3.1.1: Then with the passing of seven days, the Fortunate One, after arising from that concentration, approached the Mucalinda (tree) from the root of the Goatherd’s Banyan (tree), and after approaching the root of the Mucalinda (tree) he sat in one cross-legged posture for seven days experiencing the happiness of liberation.
pli-tv-kd1:3.2.1: Then at that time a great cloud arose out of season, (bringing) seven days of rainy weather, cold winds, and overcast days.
pli-tv-kd1:3.2.2: Then the Dragon-King Mucalinda, after leaving his domicile, and surrounding the Fortunate One’s body seven times with his coils, stood having placed his great hood above his head, (thinking):
pli-tv-kd1:3.2.3: “May the Fortunate One not be cold, may the Fortunate One not be hot, may the Fortunate One not be affected by gadflies, mosquitoes, wind, the heat (of the sun), and serpents.”
pli-tv-kd1:3.3.1: Then the Dragon-King Mucalinda, with the passing of those seven days, having understood that the sky was now clear, without a cloud, after unravelling his coils from the Fortunate One’s body, withdrawing his own form, and creating the appearance of a young brāhmaṇa, stood in front of the Fortunate One, revering the Fortunate One with raised hands.
pli-tv-kd1:3.3.2: Then the Fortunate One, having understood the significance of it, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.1: “There is happiness and detachment for the one who is satisfied, who has heard the Dhamma, and who sees,
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.3: There is happiness for him who is free from ill-will in the world,
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.4: who is restrained towards breathing beings.
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.5: The state of dispassion in the world is happiness,
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.6: the complete transcending of sense desires,
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.7: (But) for he who has removed the conceit ‘I am’ - this is indeed the highest happiness.”
pli-tv-kd1:3.4.9: The Story about Mucalinda is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:4.1.0: 4. The Story about the Royal (Tree) (Tapussa and Bhallika)
pli-tv-kd1:4.1.1: Then with the passing of seven days, the Fortunate One, after arising from that concentration, approached the Royal (tree) from the root of the Mucalinda (tree), and after approaching the root of the Royal (tree) he sat in one cross-legged posture for seven days experiencing the happiness of liberation.
pli-tv-kd1:4.2.1: Then at that time the merchants Tapussa and Ballika were in that district travelling along the highway from Ukkalā.
pli-tv-kd1:4.2.2: Then a god who had (formerly) been a blood relative of the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika said this to the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika:
pli-tv-kd1:4.2.3: “The Fortunate One, Sirs, is dwelling at the root of the Royal (tree), in the first (period) after the complete and perfect Awakening.
pli-tv-kd1:4.2.4: Go and wait upon the Fortunate One with milk-rice and honey-balls
pli-tv-kd1:4.2.5: and for a long time that will be for your benefit and happiness.”
pli-tv-kd1:4.3.1: Then the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika having taken milk-rice and honey-balls approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One they stood at one side.
pli-tv-kd1:4.3.2: While standing on one side the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:4.3.3: “Please accept our milk-rice and honey-balls, venerable Sir, Fortunate One, that for a long time will be for our benefit and happiness.”
pli-tv-kd1:4.4.1: Then it occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:4.4.2: “Realised Ones do not accept (food) in the hands,
pli-tv-kd1:4.4.3: now how can I accept the milk-rice and honey-balls?”
pli-tv-kd1:4.4.4: Then the (gods called the) Four Great Kings, knowing with their minds the reflection in the mind of the Fortunate One, brought from the four directions four bowls made of (green) stone to the Fortunate One (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:4.4.5: “Please accept, venerable Sir, Fortunate One, the milk-rice and honey-balls here (in the bowls).”
pli-tv-kd1:4.4.6: The Fortunate One accepted in the new bowl made of stone the milk-rice and honey-balls, and having accepted (it) he ate.
pli-tv-kd1:4.5.1: Then the merchants Tapussa and Bhallika said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:4.5.2: “We, venerable Sir, are those who go to the Fortunate One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, please bear in mind that we are lay disciples who have gone for refuge from today forward for as long as we have the breath of life,”
pli-tv-kd1:4.5.3: and they became the first lay disciples in the world with the two(-refuge) formula.
pli-tv-kd1:4.5.4: The Story about the Royal (tree) is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:5.1.1: Then with the passing of seven days, the Fortunate One, after arising from that concentration, approached the Goatherd’s Banyan (tree) from the root of the Royal (tree),
pli-tv-kd1:5.1.2: and there the Fortunate One dwelt at the root of the Goatherd’s Banyan (tree).
pli-tv-kd1:5.2.1: Then when the Fortunate One had gone into solitude, into seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:
pli-tv-kd1:5.2.2: “This Dhamma I have attained is deep, hard to see, hard to understand, peaceful, excellent, beyond the sphere of logic, profound, understandable (only) to the wise.
pli-tv-kd1:5.2.3: But this generation delights in desire, is devoted to desire, gladdened by desire,
pli-tv-kd1:5.2.4: and for a generation delighting in desire, devoted to desire, gladdened by desire this thing is hard to see, that is to say: conditionality and conditional origination.
pli-tv-kd1:5.2.5: This thing also is very hard to see, that is to say: the tranquilising of all processes, the letting go of all bases for cleaving, the end of craving, dispassion, cessation, Emancipation.
pli-tv-kd1:5.2.6: But if I were to teach the Dhamma and others did not understand me that would be tiring for me, that would be troublesome to me.”
pli-tv-kd1:5.3.1: Further these truly wonderful verses, unheard previously in the past, occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:5.3.2: “Now is it suitable for me to explain what was attained with difficulty?
pli-tv-kd1:5.3.4: For those overcome by passion and hatred this Dhamma is not easily understood.
pli-tv-kd1:5.3.6: Going against the stream, it is profound, deep, hard to see, subtle,
pli-tv-kd1:5.3.8: Those delighting in passion, obstructed by darkness, will not see (it).”
pli-tv-kd1:5.4.1: Such was the Fortunate One’s reflection and his mind inclined to inaction, not to teaching the Dhamma.
pli-tv-kd1:5.4.2: Then to Brahmā Sahampati, knowing with his mind the reflection in the mind of the Fortunate One, this (thought) occurred:
pli-tv-kd1:5.4.3: “The world is surely going to destruction, the world is surely going to complete destruction, wherever the Realised One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha’s mind inclines to inaction, not to teaching the Dhamma.”
pli-tv-kd1:5.5.1: Then Brahmā Sahampati, just as a strong man might stretch out a bent arm, or bend in an outstretched arm, so did he vanish from the Brahmā world and appear in front of the Fortunate One.
pli-tv-kd1:5.6.1: Then Brahmā Sahampati, after arranging his upper robe on one shoulder, placing his right knee on the earth, and raising his hands in respectful salutation, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:5.6.2: “Let the Fortunate One preach the Dhamma, venerable Sir, let the Happy One preach the Dhamma,
pli-tv-kd1:5.6.3: there are beings with little dust on the eyes who are perishing through not hearing the Dhamma, there will be those who understand the Dhamma.”
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.1: Brahmā Sahampati said this, and after saying this he said something more:
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.3: An impure Dhamma, invented by those still stained,
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.4: Open this door to the Deathless
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.5: Let them hear the Dhamma understood by the Pure One.
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.6: As one who is standing on a rock on the top of a mountain
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.7: Can see the people on all sides
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.8: In the same way, One of Great Wisdom, having ascended
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.9: The Palace made from Dhamma, Visionary One,
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.10: Look down on the people overcome by grief,
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.11: One Free of Grief, on those overcome by birth and old-age.
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.12: Rise up, O Hero, Victorious in Battle, Satthavāha Anaṇa vicara loke. Caravan-Leader, Debtless One, travel through the world.
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.14: Let the Fortunate One teach the Dhamma,
pli-tv-kd1:5.7.15: there will be those who understand.”

pli-tv-kd1:5.10.1: Then the Fortunate One, having understood Brahmā’s request, out of kindness looked at beings around the world with his Buddha-eye.
pli-tv-kd1:5.11.1: While looking around the world with his Buddha-eye the Fortunate One saw beings having little dust on the eyes, having great dust on the eyes, having sharp faculties, having undeveloped faculties, having good conditions, having poor conditions, easy to instruct, hard to instruct, and (only) some who dwelt seeing danger in what is blameworthy and in the next world.
pli-tv-kd1:5.11.2: Just as with water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses some of those water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses, born in the water, flourishing in the water, not rising above water, are nourished from inside the depths, some of those water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses, born in the water, flourishing in the water, stand level with the water, some of those water-lilies or lotuses or white lotuses, born in the water, flourishing in the water, stand above the water, and are untouched by the water.
pli-tv-kd1:5.11.3: Even so while looking around the world with his Buddha-eye the Fortunate One saw beings having little dust on the eyes, having great dust on the eyes, having sharp faculties, having undeveloped faculties, having good conditions, having poor conditions, easy to instruct, hard to instruct, and (only) some who dwelt seeing danger in what is blameworthy and in the next world,
pli-tv-kd1:5.12.1: and having seen (it) he recited this verse to Brahmā Sahampati:
pli-tv-kd1:5.12.2: “Open for you are the doors to the Deathless,
pli-tv-kd1:5.12.3: Whoever has ears let them release their faith.
pli-tv-kd1:5.12.4: Perceiving trouble, Brahmā, I did not speak amongst humans,
pli-tv-kd1:5.12.5: About what was hard-learned, the excellent Dhamma!”
pli-tv-kd1:5.13.2: “I have obtained consent for the Fortunate One to teach the Dhamma,” and after worshipping the Fortunate One, and circumambulating him, he vanished right there.
pli-tv-kd1:5.13.3: The Story about Brahmā’s request is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:6.1.1: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.1.2: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma?
pli-tv-kd1:6.1.3: Who will be able to understand the Dhamma quickly?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.1.4: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.1.5: “This Āḷāra Kālāma is wise, learned, intelligent, for a long time he has been one with little dust on his eyes.
pli-tv-kd1:6.1.6: Now what if I first teach the Dhamma to Āḷāra Kālāma? He will be able to understand the Dhamma quickly.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.2.1: Then an invisible god informed the Fortunate One: “Āḷāra Kālāma died seven days ago, venerable Sir,”
pli-tv-kd1:6.2.2: and this knowledge arose in the Fortunate One: “Āḷāra Kālāma died seven days ago.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.2.3: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.2.5: if he had heard this Dhamma he would have understood it quickly.”

pli-tv-kd1:6.3.3: Who will be able to understand the Dhamma quickly?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.3.4: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.3.5: “This Uddaka Rāmaputta is wise, learned, intelligent, for a long time he has been one with little dust on his eyes.
pli-tv-kd1:6.3.6: Now, what if I first teach the Dhamma to Uddaka Rāmaputta? He will be able to understand the Dhamma quickly.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.4.1: Then an invisible god informed the Fortunate One: “Uddaka Rāmaputta died yesterday evening, venerable Sir,”
pli-tv-kd1:6.4.2: and this knowledge arose in the Fortunate One: “Uddaka Rāmaputta died yesterday evening.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.4.3: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.4.5: if he had heard this Dhamma he would have understood it quickly.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.5.1: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.5.2: “To whom should I first teach the Dhamma?
pli-tv-kd1:6.5.3: Who will be able to understand the Dhamma quickly?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.5.4: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.5.5: “The group-of-five monks were very helpful to me, they attended on me when I was striving resolutely.
pli-tv-kd1:6.6.1: Now, what if I first teach the Dhamma to the group-of-five monks?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.6.2: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.6.3: “Where are the group-of-five monks dwelling now?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.6.4: The Fortunate One saw with the divine eye which is purified and surpasses that of (normal) men that the group-of-five monks were dwelling near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana.
pli-tv-kd1:6.6.5: Then the Fortunate One, having dwelt for as long as he liked left on walking tour for Bārāṇasī.
pli-tv-kd1:6.7.1: The Abstainer Upaka saw the Fortunate One going along the highway between the Bodhi (tree) and Gayā, and after seeing (him), he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.7.2: “Your faculties, friend, are very clear, purified is your skin and bright,
pli-tv-kd1:6.7.3: on account of whom, friend, did you go forth
pli-tv-kd1:6.7.5: or what Dhamma do you prefer?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.1: After this was said, the Fortunate One addressed the Abstainer Upaka with verses:
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.3: Undefiled in regard to all things,
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.4: Having given up everything, liberated through the destruction of craving,
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.5: Having deep knowledge myself, who should I point to (as Teacher)?
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.6: There is no Teacher for me,
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.7: no one like me is found,
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.8: There is no person equal to me in the world with its gods.
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.10: I am a Worthy One in the world, I am the Unsurpassed Teacher,
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.12: I am the One Perfect Sambuddha, cool and passionless.
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.14: I go to Kāsī’s city to set the Dhamma-Wheel rolling,
pli-tv-kd1:6.8.16: I will beat the drum of the Deathless in a world that is blind.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.9.1: “It is as if you claim, friend, you are a Worthy One, an Infinite Victor!”
pli-tv-kd1:6.9.3: who have attained the destruction of the pollutants.
pli-tv-kd1:6.9.4: I have been victorious over all wicked things, therefore, Upaka, I am a Victor.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.9.5: When this was said, the Abstainer Upaka, after saying: “It may be so, friend,”
pli-tv-kd1:6.9.6: shaking his head, and taking the wrong path, went away.
pli-tv-kd1:6.10.1: Then the Fortunate One, while walking gradually on walking tour approached Bārāṇasī and the group-of-five monks at the Deer Park in Isipatana.
pli-tv-kd1:6.10.2: The group-of-five monks saw the Fortunate One coming from afar
pli-tv-kd1:6.10.3: and after seeing (him), they resolved among themselves (on this course of action):
pli-tv-kd1:6.10.4: “This Ascetic Gotama who is coming, friends, is given to luxury, forsaking the striving he has gone back to luxury.
pli-tv-kd1:6.10.5: He should certainly not be worshipped or stood up for, nor should his bowl and robe be taken,
pli-tv-kd1:6.10.6: however, we can prepare a seat - if he wishes he will sit down.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.11.1: As the Fortunate One approached the group-of-five monks, the group-of-five monks were unable to continue with their own agreement,
pli-tv-kd1:6.11.2: and after going out to meet the Fortunate One, one of them took the Fortunate One’s bowl and robe, one prepared the seat, one placed the water (for washing) the feet, the foot-stool, and the foot-stand,
pli-tv-kd1:6.11.3: and the Fortunate One sat down on the prepared seat,
pli-tv-kd1:6.11.4: and while sitting the Fortunate One washed his feet.
pli-tv-kd1:6.11.5: Then they addressed the Fortunate One by name and by the word ‘friend’.
pli-tv-kd1:6.12.1: After this was said, the Fortunate One said this to the group-of-five monks:
pli-tv-kd1:6.12.2: “Do not address the Fortunate One by name, monks, and by the word ‘friend’,
pli-tv-kd1:6.12.3: the Realised One is a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha, lend an ear, monks, I will instruct you about the attainment of the Deathless, I will teach the Dhamma,
pli-tv-kd1:6.12.4: (and) following the path as it has been preached, after no long time you will (attain) that good for which young men of good family
pli-tv-kd1:6.12.5: rightly go forth from the home to the homeless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life,
pli-tv-kd1:6.12.6: and will dwell having known, experienced, and attained it yourselves in this very life.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.13.1: After this was said, the group-of-five monks said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.13.2: “But you, friend Gotama, by that (ascetic) lifestyle, that practice, that difficult way of living, did not arrive at a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight. So how can you now, given to luxury, forsaking the striving, gone back to luxury, attain a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.1: After this was said, the Fortunate One said this to the group-of-five monks:
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.2: “The Realised One, monks, is not given to luxury, is not forsaking the striving, and has not gone back to luxury.
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.3: The Realised One is a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha,
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.4: lend an ear, monks, I will instruct you about the attainment of the Deathless,
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.5: I will teach the Dhamma, (and) following the path as it has been preached, after no long time (you will attain) that good for which young men of good family
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.6: rightly go forth from the home to the homeless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life,
pli-tv-kd1:6.14.7: and will dwell having known, experienced, and attained it yourselves in this very life.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.15.1: For a second time the group-of-five monks said this to the Fortunate One: “But you, friend Gotama, by that (ascetic) lifestyle, that practice, that difficult way of living, did not arrive at a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight. So how can you now, given to luxury, forsaking the striving, gone back to luxury, attain a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.15.2: For a second time, the Fortunate One said this to the group-of-five monks: “The Realised One, monks, is not given to luxury, is not forsaking the striving, and has not gone back to luxury. The Realised One is a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha, lend an ear, monks, I will instruct you about the attainment of the Deathless, I will teach the Dhamma, (and) following the path as it has been preached, after no long time (you will attain) that good for which young men of good family rightly go forth from the home to the homeless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life, and will dwell having known, experienced, and attained it yourself in this very life.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.15.3: For a third time the group-of-five monks said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.15.4: “But you, friend Gotama, by that (ascetic) lifestyle, that practice, that difficult way of living, did not arrive at a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight. So how can you now, given to luxury, forsaking the striving, gone back to luxury, attain a state beyond (ordinary) human beings, a distinction of what is truly noble knowledge and insight?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.1: After this was said, the Fortunate One said this to the group-of-five monks:
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.2: “Are you aware of my having spoken to you like this before?”
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.4: “The Realised One is a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha, lend an ear, monks, I will instruct you about the attainment of the Deathless,
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.5: I will teach the Dhamma, (and) following the path as it has been preached, after no long time (you will attain) that good for which young men of good family
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.6: rightly go forth from the home to the homeless life, that unsurpassed conclusion to the spiritual life,
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.7: and will dwell having known, experienced, and attained it yourself in this very life,”
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.8: and the Fortunate One was able to persuade the group-of-five monks.
pli-tv-kd1:6.16.9: Then the group-of-five monks listened to the Fortunate One, they lent an ear, (so as) to attend with their mind to deep knowledge.
pli-tv-kd1:6.17.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the group-of-five monks, saying:
pli-tv-kd1:6.17.2: “There are these two extremes, monks, that one who has gone forth ought not to associate with,
pli-tv-kd1:6.17.4: which is this: devotion and clinging to the pleasure in sense pleasures, which is low, vulgar, worldly, ignoble, and not connected with the goal; and this: devotion to self-mortification, which is painful, ignoble, and not connected with the goal.
pli-tv-kd1:6.17.5: Not having approached either of these two extremes, monks, the middle practice was awakened to by the Realised One, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and which leads to peace, deep knowledge, Complete Awakening, and Emancipation. Now what is this middle practice, monks, that was awakened to by the Realised One, which produces vision, produces knowledge,
pli-tv-kd1:6.18.1: and which leads to peace, deep knowledge, Complete Awakening, and Emancipation?
pli-tv-kd1:6.18.2: It is this Eightfold Noble Path, as follows:
pli-tv-kd1:6.18.3: right view right thought right speech right action right livelihood right endeavour right mindfulness right concentration.
pli-tv-kd1:6.18.4: This is the middle practice, monks, that was awakened to by the Realised One, which produces vision, produces knowledge, and which leads to peace, deep knowledge, Complete Awakening, and Emancipation.
pli-tv-kd1:6.19.1: Now this, monks, is the noble truth of suffering:
pli-tv-kd1:6.19.2: birth is suffering also old age is suffering also sickness is suffering also death is suffering being joined to what is not dear is suffering being separated from what is dear is suffering also not to obtain what one longs for is suffering
pli-tv-kd1:6.19.3: in brief, the five constituent parts (of mind and body) that provide fuel for attachment are suffering.
pli-tv-kd1:6.20.1: Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the arising of suffering:
pli-tv-kd1:6.20.2: it is that craving which leads to continuation in existence, which is connected with enjoyment and passion, greatly enjoying this and that, as follows:
pli-tv-kd1:6.20.3: craving for sense pleasures craving for continuation craving for discontinuation.
pli-tv-kd1:6.21.1: Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering:
pli-tv-kd1:6.21.2: it is the complete fading away and cessation without remainder of that craving - liberation, letting go, release, and non-adherence.
pli-tv-kd1:6.22.1: Now this, monks, is the noble truth of the practice leading to the end of suffering,
pli-tv-kd1:6.22.2: it is this Eightfold Noble Path, as follows:
pli-tv-kd1:6.22.3: right view right thought right speech right action right livelihood right endeavour right mindfulness right concentration.
pli-tv-kd1:6.23.1: “This is the noble truth of suffering” - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose, light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of suffering” refers (i.e. suffering itself) ought to be fully known - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose, light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of suffering” refers has been fully known - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.23.3: light arose. “This is the noble truth of the arising of suffering” - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.24.1: light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of the arising of suffering” refers (i.e. craving) ought to be given up - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose, light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of the arising of suffering” refers has been given up, to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.24.3: light arose. “This is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering” - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.25.1: light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering” refers (i.e. Emancipation) ought to be experienced - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose, light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of the cessation of suffering” refers has been experienced - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.25.3: light arose. “This is the noble truth of the practice going to the cessation of suffering” - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.26.1: light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of the practice leading to the end of suffering” refers (i.e. the practice itself) ought to be developed - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose, understanding arose, light arose. Now that to which “this is the noble truth of the practice leading to the end of suffering” refers has been developed - to me, monks, regarding these previously unheard-of things vision arose, knowledge arose, wisdom arose,
pli-tv-kd1:6.27.1: For as long as to me, monks, in regard to these four noble truths - turned like this, in three ways, twelvefold - knowledge and insight as it really is was not quite clear, for that long, monks, I did not declare to the world with its gods, Māra, and Brahmā, to this generation, with its ascetics and brāhmaṇas, princes and men, that I was a Full and Perfect Sambuddha with unsurpassed complete awakening. But when to me, monks, in regard to these four noble truths - turned like this, in three ways, twelvefold - knowledge and insight as it really is was quite clear then, monks, I did declare to the world with its gods, Māra, and Brahmā, to this generation, with its ascetics and brāhmaṇas, princes and men,
pli-tv-kd1:6.28.1: that I was a Full and Perfect Sambuddha with unsurpassed complete awakening.
pli-tv-kd1:6.29.1: To me knowledge and insight arose: Sure is my liberation of mind
pli-tv-kd1:6.29.2: this is my last birth now there is no continuation of existence.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.29.3: The Fortunate One said this, and the group-of-five monks were uplifted and greatly rejoiced in what was said by the Fortunate One.
pli-tv-kd1:6.29.4: Moreover, as this sermon was being given, to the venerable Koṇḍañña the dust-free, stainless, Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:6.29.5: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.1: Now when the Dhamma Wheel was set rolling by the Fortunate One the Earth gods let loose a cry:
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.2: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Having heard the cry of the Earth gods the gods called the Four Great Kings let loose a cry: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.3: Having heard the cry of the gods called the Four Great Kings the Tāvatiṁsa gods let loose a cry: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.4: Having heard the cry of the Tāvatiṁsa gods
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.5: the Yāma gods let loose a cry: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Having heard the cry of the Yāma gods
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.6: the Tusita gods let loose a cry: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Having heard the cry of the Tusita gods
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.7: the Nimmāṇarati gods let loose a cry: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Having heard the cry of the Nimmāṇarati gods
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.8: the Paranimmitavasavatti gods let loose a cry: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or by a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.” Having heard the cry of the Paranimmitavasavatti gods
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.9: the Brahmakāyika gods let loose a cry:
pli-tv-kd1:6.30.10: “Near Bārāṇasī, in the Deer Park at Isipatana, the unsurpassed Dhamma Wheel has been set rolling by the Fortunate One, and it cannot be rolled back by an ascetic or a brāhmaṇa or by a god or by a Māra or by a Brahmā or by anyone in the world.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.31.1: Thus at that moment, at that second, that cry reached as far as the Brahmā worlds,
pli-tv-kd1:6.31.2: and this ten-thousand world-element moved, wavered, and shook,
pli-tv-kd1:6.31.3: and great and measureless light became manifest in the world, transcending the godly power of the gods.
pli-tv-kd1:6.31.4: Then the Fortunate One uttered this inspired utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:6.31.6: Thus to the venerable Koṇḍañña came the name Aññā Koṇḍañña (Koṇḍañña, he-who-knows).
pli-tv-kd1:6.32.1: Then the venerable Aññā Koṇḍañña, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.32.2: “May I receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may I receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.32.3: “Come, monk,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:6.32.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.32.5: That was this the venerable one’s full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:6.33.1: Then the Fortunate One gave advice and instruction with a Dhamma talk to the remaining monks.
pli-tv-kd1:6.33.2: Then to the venerable Vappa and to the venerable Bhaddiya as the Fortunate One gave advice and instruction with a Dhamma talk the dust-free, stainless, Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:6.33.3: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.34.1: They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.34.2: “May we receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may we receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.34.3: “Come, monks,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:6.34.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.34.5: That was these venerable ones’ full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:6.35.1: Then the Fortunate One, living on (those three) monks’ food gave advice and instruction with a Dhamma talk to the remaining monks,
pli-tv-kd1:6.35.2: and the six monks subsisted on whatever, after walking for alms-food, the three monks brought them.
pli-tv-kd1:6.36.1: Then to the venerable Mahānāma and to the venerable Assaji as the Fortunate One gave advice and instruction with a Dhamma talk the dust-free, stainless, Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:6.36.2: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.37.1: They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:6.37.2: “May we receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may we receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.37.3: “Come, monks,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:6.37.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:6.37.5: That was these venerable ones’ full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:6.38.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the group-of-five monks (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:6.38.3: for if this bodily form, monks, were Self this bodily form would not lead to affliction, and regarding bodily form it might be possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.38.4: ‘Let my bodily form be thus, let my bodily form be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.38.5: But because bodily form, monks, is not Self, therefore bodily form does lead to affliction, and regarding bodily form it is not possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.38.6: ‘Let my bodily form be thus, let my bodily form be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.39.2: for if this feeling, monks, were Self this feeling would not lead to affliction, and regarding feeling it might be possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.39.3: ‘Let my feeling be thus, let my feeling be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.39.4: But because feeling, monks, is not Self, therefore feeling does lead to affliction, and regarding feeling it is not possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.39.5: ‘Let my feeling be thus, let my feeling be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.2: for if this perception, monks, were Self this perception would not lead to affliction, and regarding perception it might be possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.3: ‘Let my perception be thus, let my perception be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.4: But because perception, monks, is not Self, therefore perception does lead to affliction, and regarding perception it is not possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.5: ‘Let my perception be thus, let my perception be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.7: for if these (mental) processes, monks, were Self these (mental) processes would not lead to affliction, and regarding (mental) processes it might be possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.8: ‘Let my (mental) processes be thus, let my (mental) processes be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.9: But because (mental) processes, monks, are not Self, therefore (mental) processes do lead to affliction, and regarding (mental) processes it is not possible (to say):
pli-tv-kd1:6.40.10: ‘Let my (mental) processes be thus, let my (mental) processes be not thus.’
pli-tv-kd1:6.41.2: for if this consciousness, monks, were Self this consciousness would not lead to affliction, and regarding consciousness it might be possible (to say):

pli-tv-kd1:7.1.1: Then at that time at Bārāṇasī there was a delicate young man of good family, Yasa by name, a merchant’s son.
pli-tv-kd1:7.1.2: There were three palaces for him: one for the winter time, one for the summer time, and one for the rainy season.
pli-tv-kd1:7.1.4: During the four months in the rainy season palace, while a female musical ensemble was entertaining him, he did not descend to the bottom of the palace.
pli-tv-kd1:7.2.1: Then while the young man Yasa, possessed of and endowed with the five strands of sensual pleasure, was being entertained he fell asleep first, and his retinue fell asleep afterwards, and all night an oil-lamp burned.
pli-tv-kd1:7.2.2: Then the young man Yasa, after waking first, saw his retinue sleeping,
pli-tv-kd1:7.2.3: one with a lute in her armpit, another with a small drum on her neck, another with a drum on her chest, another with hair dishevelled, another dribbling, another muttering, (so that) it seemed as if there was a cemetery close at hand.
pli-tv-kd1:7.2.4: Having seen (this) the danger became clear to him, and his mind was established in world-weariness.
pli-tv-kd1:7.2.5: Then the young man Yasa uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:7.3.1: Then the young man Yasa, after donning his golden slippers, went to the door of his dwelling.
pli-tv-kd1:7.3.3: o “Let there be no obstacle to the going-forth of the young man Yasa from the home to the homeless life.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.3.4: Then the young man Yasa went to the city gate.
pli-tv-kd1:7.3.6: o “Let there be no obstacle to the going-forth of the young man Yasa from the home to the homeless life.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.3.7: Then the young man Yasa approached the Deer Park at Isipatana.
pli-tv-kd1:7.4.1: Then at that time, towards the time of dawn, after rising, the Fortunate One was walking in the open air.
pli-tv-kd1:7.4.2: The Fortunate One saw the young man Yasa coming while still far away, and after seeing (him) and descending from the walkway, he sat down on the prepared seat.
pli-tv-kd1:7.4.3: Then the young man Yasa, not far from the Fortunate One uttered this exalted utterance:
pli-tv-kd1:7.4.5: Then the Fortunate One said this to the young man Yasa:
pli-tv-kd1:7.4.6: “This, Yasa, is not tribulation, this is not ruination,
pli-tv-kd1:7.4.7: come, Yasa, sit down and I will teach Dhamma to you.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.5.1: Then the young man Yasa (thinking): ‘It seems this is not tribulation, this is not ruination’,
pli-tv-kd1:7.5.2: joyful, uplifted, after taking off his golden slippers, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:7.5.3: To the young man Yasa, sitting at one side, the Fortunate One spoke about the gradual teaching, that is to say: talk about giving, talk about virtue, talk about heaven,
pli-tv-kd1:7.5.4: the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual desires, and the advantages of renunciation, (these) he explained.
pli-tv-kd1:7.6.1: When the Fortunate One knew that the young man Yasa had a ready mind, a pliable mind, an open mind, an uplifted mind, a confident mind, he explained to him the Dhamma teaching the Awakened Ones have discovered themselves:
pli-tv-kd1:7.6.3: Just as it is known that a clean cloth without a stain will take the dye well,
pli-tv-kd1:7.6.4: just so to the young man Yasa on that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:7.6.5: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.7.1: Then the young man Yasa’s mother, having ascended the palace, and not finding the young man Yasa approached the merchant householder, and after approaching the merchant householder, she said this:
pli-tv-kd1:7.7.2: “Your son Yasa, householder, cannot be found.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.7.3: Then the merchant householder, after sending scouts on horses to the four directions, himself approached the Deer Park at Isipatana.
pli-tv-kd1:7.7.4: The merchant householder saw the cast-off golden sandals, and after seeing (them) he went after him.
pli-tv-kd1:7.8.1: The Fortunate One saw the merchant householder, coming while still far away, and after seeing (him), this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:7.8.2: “Now what if I were to so arrange it with my psychic powers that while the merchant householder is sitting here he could not see the young man Yasa sitting here?”
pli-tv-kd1:7.8.3: Then the Fortunate One so arranged it with his psychic powers.
pli-tv-kd1:7.9.1: Then the merchant householder approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:7.9.2: “Has the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, seen the young man Yasa?”
pli-tv-kd1:7.9.3: “Sit, householder, and it may be that while you are sitting here you will see the young man Yasa sitting here.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.9.5: “It seems that while sitting here I will see the young man Yasa sitting here,” and joyful, uplifted, after worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.1: To the merchant householder, sitting at one side the Fortunate One spoke about the gradual teaching, that is to say: talk about giving, talk about virtue, talk about heaven,

pli-tv-kd1:7.10.3: When the Fortunate One knew that the merchant householder had a ready mind, a pliable mind, an open mind, an uplifted mind, a confident mind, he explained to him the Dhamma teaching the Awakened Ones have discovered themselves:
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.5: Just as it is known that a clean cloth without a stain will take the dye well,
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.6: just so to the merchant householder on that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.7: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.8: Then the merchant householder, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.10: Just as, venerable Sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost,
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.11: or carry an oil lamp into the darkness, (thinking): ‘those with vision will see forms’,
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.12: just so has the Dhamma been explained by the Fortunate One in countless ways.
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.13: I go, venerable Sir, to the Fortunate One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Community of monks.
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.14: Please bear it in mind, Fortunate One, that I am a lay follower who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I have the breath of life,”
pli-tv-kd1:7.10.15: and he became the first lay disciple in the world with the three(-refuge) formula.
pli-tv-kd1:7.11.1: Then while Dhamma was being taught to the young man Yasa’s father as (Yasa) was reflecting on the stage (he had reached), just as it was seen, as it was understood, his mind was liberated from the pollutants without attachment.
pli-tv-kd1:7.11.2: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:7.11.3: “While Dhamma was being taught to the young man Yasa’s father as (Yasa) was reflecting on the stage (he had reached), just as it was seen, as it was understood, his mind was liberated from the pollutants without attachment.
pli-tv-kd1:7.11.4: It is impossible that the young man Yasa could go back to enjoying the low life of sensual pleasures in the way he formerly did when he was at home.
pli-tv-kd1:7.11.5: Now what if I were to allay my psychic powers?”
pli-tv-kd1:7.11.6: Then the Fortunate One allayed his psychic powers.
pli-tv-kd1:7.12.1: Then the merchant householder saw the young man Yasa sitting (there), and after seeing (him), he said this to the young man Yasa:
pli-tv-kd1:7.12.2: “Your Mother, dear Yasa, is taken up with lamenting and grieving, give life to your Mother!”
pli-tv-kd1:7.13.1: Then the young man Yasa looked up at the Fortunate One.
pli-tv-kd1:7.13.2: Then the Fortunate One said this to the merchant householder:
pli-tv-kd1:7.13.3: “What do you think of this, householder, for the young man Yasa, with a trainee’s knowledge, with a trainee’s insight, who saw the Dhamma, just as you have, (but) as he was reflecting on the stage (he had reached), just as it was seen, as it was understood, his mind was liberated from the pollutants without attachment.
pli-tv-kd1:7.13.4: Is it possible that he could go back to enjoying the low life of sensual pleasures in the way he formerly did when he was at home?”
pli-tv-kd1:7.13.6: “But for the young man Yasa, householder, with a trainee’s knowledge, with a trainee’s insight, he saw the Dhamma, just as you have, (and) as he was reflecting on the stage (he had reached), just as it was seen, as it was understood, his mind was liberated from the pollutants without attachment.
pli-tv-kd1:7.13.7: It is impossible that the young man Yasa could go back to enjoying the low life of sensual pleasures in the way he formerly did when he was at home.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.14.1: “It is a gain for the young man Yasa, venerable Sir, it is a great gain, venerable Sir, for the young man Yasa, that the young man Yasa’s mind is liberated from the pollutants without attachment.
pli-tv-kd1:7.14.2: May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, consent to me (offering him) a meal today, together with the young man Yasa as the ascetic who attends on him.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.14.3: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.
pli-tv-kd1:7.14.4: Then the merchant householder, having understood the Fortunate One’s consent, having worshipped and circumambulated the Fortunate One, went away.
pli-tv-kd1:7.15.1: Then the young man Yasa not long after the merchant householder had gone away said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:7.15.2: “May I receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may I receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.15.3: “Come, monk,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:7.15.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:7.15.5: That was this venerable one’s full ordination,
pli-tv-kd1:7.15.6: and at that time there were seven Worthy Ones in the world.
pli-tv-kd1:8.1.1: Then the Fortunate One, after dressing in the morning time, and picking up his bowl and robe, went with the venerable Yasa as the ascetic who attends on him to the merchant householder’s home, and after approaching he sat down on the prepared seat.
pli-tv-kd1:8.1.2: Then the venerable Yasa’s Mother and his former wife approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side.

pli-tv-kd1:8.3.1: They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:8.3.2: “Excellent, venerable Sir! Excellent, venerable Sir! pli-tv-kd1:8.3.3: We go, venerable Sir, to the Fortunate One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Community of monks.
pli-tv-kd1:8.3.4: Please bear it in mind, Fortunate One, that we are female lay followers who have gone for refuge from today forward for as long as we have the breath of life,”
pli-tv-kd1:8.3.5: and they became the first female lay disciples in the world with the three(-refuge) formula.
pli-tv-kd1:8.4.1: Then Yasa’s Mother and Father and former wife having with their own hands served and satisfied the Fortunate One and the venerable Yasa with excellent food and drinks, when the Fortunate One had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:8.4.2: Then the Fortunate One, after Yasa’s Mother and Father and former wife o had been instructed, roused, enthused, and cheered with a Dhamma talk, having risen from the seat, went away.

pli-tv-kd1:9.1.2: (named) Vimala, Subāhu, Puṇṇaji and Gavampati heard:

pli-tv-kd1:9.1.5: “This is not an inferior Dhamma and Discipline, not an inferior going-forth in which the young man Yasa, after shaving off his hair and beard, and donning brown garments, has gone forth from the home to the homeless life.”

pli-tv-kd1:11.1.1: Then the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.2: “I am liberated from all snares, monks, both divine and human,
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.3: you are also liberated from all snares, monks, both divine and human.
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.4: Go on a walk, monks, for the benefit of many people, for the happiness of many people, out of compassion for the world, for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of gods and men.
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.5: Do not let two go by one (way), teach the Dhamma, monks,
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.6: (which is) good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end, with its meaning, with its (proper) phrasing; explain the spiritual life which is complete, full and pure,
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.7: there are beings with little dust on the eyes who are perishing through not hearing the Dhamma, there will be those who will understand the Dhamma.
pli-tv-kd1:11.1.8: I will go, monks, to Uruvelā and Senāni Village in order to teach the Dhamma.”
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.1: Then the Wicked Māra approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching the Fortunate One he spoke this verse:
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.2: “You are bound with all the snares, both divine and human,
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.4: You are bound in great bonds, you are not free from me, ascetic!”
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.6: “I am liberated from all snares, both divine and human,
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.8: I am liberated from the great bonds: you are brought low, End-Maker!”
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.10: “The snare is in the very space the mind travels through,
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.12: Therefore it is in bondage, you are not free from me, ascetic!”
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.14: “Forms, sounds, scents, tastes, tangibles delight the mind,
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.16: (But) for me there is no desire: you are brought low, End-Maker!”
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.18: Then the Wicked Māra (understood): “The Fortunate One knows me, the Happy One knows me!”
pli-tv-kd1:11.2.19: and pained, depressed, he vanished right there.

pli-tv-kd1:12.1.1: Then at that time monks from various districts, from various states, were bringing those seeking the going-forth and seeking the full ordination, (thinking):
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.2: “The Fortunate One will give these the going-forth, will give them full ordination,”
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.3: and therefore the monks became tired, as did also those seeking the going-forth and seeking the full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.4: Then when the Fortunate One had gone into solitude, into seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.5: “Now monks from various districts, from various states, bring those seeking the going-forth and seeking the full ordination, (thinking):
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.6: ‘The Fortunate One will give these the going-forth, will give them full ordination,’
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.7: and therefore the monks become tired, as do also those seeking the going-forth and seeking the full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.8: What if I were to give permission to the monks, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:12.1.9: ‘Now you, monks, in whatever district, in whatever state, may give the going-forth, may give the full ordination'?”
pli-tv-kd1:12.2.1: Then the Fortunate One, having risen from seclusion in the evening time, for this cause, for this reason, after assembling the Community of monks, and giving them a talk on Dhamma, addressed the monks (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:12.2.2: “Here, monks, having gone into solitude, into seclusion, this reflection arose in my mind:
pli-tv-kd1:12.2.3: ‘Now monks from various districts, from various states, bring those seeking the going-forth and seeking the full ordination, (thinking):
pli-tv-kd1:12.2.4: “The Fortunate One will give these the going-forth, will give them full ordination,” and therefore the monks became tired, as also do those seeking the going-forth and seeking the full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:12.3.1: What if I were to give permission to the monks, (saying): “Now you, monks, in whatever district, in whatever state, may give the going-forth, may give the full ordination”?’ Now I give permission to you, monks, in whatever district, in whatever state, you may give the going-forth, may give the full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:12.3.2: And in this way, monks, you should give the going-forth, should give the full ordination:
pli-tv-kd1:12.3.3: first, after making them shave off hair and beard, don brown garments, arrange the upper robe on one shoulder, worship the monks’ feet, sit on their heels, and holding their hands in respectful salutation, you should say to them, speak thus:
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.1: ‘I go to the Buddha for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.2: I go to the Dhamma for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.3: I go to the Sangha for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.4: For a second time I go to the Buddha for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.5: For a second time I go to the Dhamma for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.6: For a second time I go to the Sangha for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.7: For a third time I go to the Buddha for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.8: For a third time I go to the Dhamma for refuge
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.9: For a third time I go to the Sangha for refuge.’
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.10: I give permission, monks, for the going-forth and the full ordination through going to the three refuges.”
pli-tv-kd1:12.4.11: The Story of Full Ordination through Going to the Three Refuges is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:13.1.1: Then the Fortunate One, having stayed for the Rains Retreat, addressed the monks, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:13.1.2: “I, monks, through wise application of thought, through wise endeavour, have attained supreme liberation, have experienced supreme liberation;
pli-tv-kd1:13.1.3: you also, monks, through wise application of thought, through wise endeavour, have attained supreme liberation, have experienced supreme liberation.”

pli-tv-kd1:13.2.2: “You are bound with Māra’s snares, both divine and human,
pli-tv-kd1:13.2.4: You are bound in Māra’s bonds, you are not free from me, ascetic!”
pli-tv-kd1:13.2.6: “I am liberated from Māra’s snares, both divine and human,
pli-tv-kd1:13.2.8: I am liberated from Māra’s bonds: you are brought low, End-Maker!”
pli-tv-kd1:13.2.10: Then the Wicked Māra (understood): “The Fortunate One knows me, the Happy One knows me!”
