pli-tv-kd1:14.1.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dwelt in Bārāṇasī as long as he liked, left on a walking tour for Uruvelā.
pli-tv-kd1:14.1.2: Then the Fortunate One, having gone down from the road, approached a certain jungle thicket, and after approaching and entering that jungle thicket, he sat down at the root of a certain tree.
pli-tv-kd1:14.1.3: Then at that time a group of thirty good friends, together with their wives, were amusing themselves in that jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:14.1.4: One, who was not married, had for that reason brought along a harlot.
pli-tv-kd1:14.1.6: Then that harlot, while they were amusing themselves heedlessly, having taken his belongings, ran away.
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.1: Then those friends, doing their friend a service, were searching for that woman and wandering around in that jungle thicket. They saw the Fortunate One sitting at the root of a certain tree,
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.2: and after seeing (him) they approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching they said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.3: “Can the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, see a woman?”
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.4: “But why, young men, (look for) a woman?”
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.5: “Here, venerable Sir, we, a group of thirty good friends, together with our wives, were amusing ourselves in this jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.6: One, who was not married, had for that reason brought along a harlot.
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.8: Then that harlot, venerable Sir, while we were amusing ourselves heedlessly, having taken his belongings, ran away.
pli-tv-kd1:14.2.9: Therefore we, venerable Sir, doing our friend a service, are searching for that woman and wandering around in this jungle thicket.”
pli-tv-kd1:14.3.1: “What do you think of this, young men, what is better for you:
pli-tv-kd1:14.3.2: that you should search for a woman, or that you should search for yourselves?”
pli-tv-kd1:14.3.3: “This is better for us, venerable Sir, that we should search for ourselves.”
pli-tv-kd1:14.3.4: “Then, young men, be seated, I will teach the Dhamma to you.”
pli-tv-kd1:14.3.5: “Certainly, venerable Sir,” said that group of good friends, and after worshipping the Fortunate One, they sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:14.4.1: The Fortunate One spoke about the gradual teaching to them, that is to say: talk about giving, talk about virtue, talk about heaven,
pli-tv-kd1:14.4.2: the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual desires, and the advantages of renunciation, (these) he explained.
pli-tv-kd1:14.4.3: When the Fortunate One knew that they had ready minds, pliable minds, open minds, uplifted minds, confident minds, he explained to them the Dhamma teaching the Awakened Ones have discovered themselves: Suffering, Origination, Cessation, Path.
pli-tv-kd1:14.4.4: Just as it is known that a clean cloth without a stain will take the dye well,
pli-tv-kd1:14.4.5: just so to them on that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:14.4.6: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.1: They, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.2: “May we receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may we receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.3: “Come, monks,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.5: That was these venerable ones’ full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.6: The Tale of the Good Group of Friends is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:14.5.7: The Second Section for Recital [is Finished]
pli-tv-kd1:15.1.1: Then the Fortunate One while walking gradually on walking tour arrived at Uruvelā.
pli-tv-kd1:15.1.2: Then at that time at Uruvelā there lived three yogis:
pli-tv-kd1:15.1.3: known as Uruvelakassapa, Nadīkassapa, and Gayākassapa.
pli-tv-kd1:15.1.4: Of these, the yogi Uruvelakassapa was the leader, guide, chief, director, and instructor of five hundred yogis.
pli-tv-kd1:15.1.5: The yogi Nadīkassapa was the leader,
pli-tv-kd1:15.1.6: guide, chief, director, and instructor of three hundred yogis. The yogi Gayākassapa was the leader, guide, chief, director, and instructor of two hundred yogis.
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.1: Then the Fortunate One approached the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s ashram, and after approaching he said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.2: “If it is not troublesome to you, Kassapa, we would stay for one night in the sacrificial firehouse.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.3: “It is not troublesome to me, Great Ascetic, (but) there is a fierce, venomous, poisonous, Dragon-King here, having psychic power, he should not (be allowed to) harass you.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.4: For a second time the Fortunate One said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.5: “If it is not troublesome to you, Kassapa, we would stay for one night in the sacrificial firehouse.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.6: “It is not troublesome to me, Great Ascetic, (but) there is a fierce, venomous, poisonous, Dragon-King here, having psychic power, he should not (be allowed to) harass you.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.7: For a third time the Fortunate One said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.8: “If it is not troublesome to you, Kassapa, we would stay for one night in the sacrificial firehouse.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.9: “It is not troublesome to me, Great Ascetic, (but) there is a fierce, venomous, poisonous, Dragon-King here, having psychic power, he should not (be allowed to) harass you.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.10: “It is all right, he will not harass me, come now, Kassapa, allow me the sacrificial firehouse.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.2.11: “Dwell (there), Great Ascetic, according to your pleasure.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.3.1: Then the Fortunate One, after entering the sacrificial firehouse and preparing a grass covering, sat down, folded his legs crosswise, set his body straight, and established mindfulness at the front.
pli-tv-kd1:15.3.2: Then the Dragon saw that the Fortunate One had entered, and after seeing (him), pained, depressed, he belched out smoke.
pli-tv-kd1:15.3.3: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:15.3.4: “Now what if I, without having destroyed this Dragon’s tegument, skin, flesh, muscle, bone, or bone-marrow, were to overcome (the Dragon’s) power with (my) power?”
pli-tv-kd1:15.4.1: Then the Fortunate One so arranged it with his psychic powers that he (also) belched out smoke.
pli-tv-kd1:15.4.2: Then that Dragon, unbearably angry, blazed forth.
pli-tv-kd1:15.4.3: The Fortunate One, having attained the fire-element, also blazed forth,
pli-tv-kd1:15.4.4: and both of them burned so bright that it was as if the sacrificial firehouse on fire, in flames, was burning down.
pli-tv-kd1:15.4.5: Then those yogis, having surrounded the sacrificial firehouse, said this:
pli-tv-kd1:15.4.6: “The Great Ascetic is surely intelligent, but he is harassed by the Dragon.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.5.1: Then the Fortunate One, with the passing of that night, without harming that Dragon’s tegument, skin, flesh, muscle, bone, or bone-marrow, after overcoming (the Dragon’s) power with (his own) power and dropping him into his bowl, showed (him) to the yogi Uruvelakassapa, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:15.5.2: “This is your Dragon, Kassapa, his power was overcome by (my) power.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.5.3: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:15.5.4: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since he can overcome this fierce, venomous, poisonous, Dragon-King’s psychic power with (his own) power, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.1: Near the (river) Nerañjarā the Fortunate One said this to Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.3: “If it is not troublesome to you, Kassapa, we would live for this moonlight night in the fire shelter.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.5: “It is not troublesome to me, Great Ascetic, but seeking your comfort I (would) prevent you,
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.8: (For) there is a fierce, venomous, poisonous, Dragon-King here, having psychic power - he should not (be allowed to) harass you!”
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.10: “It is all right, he will not harass me, come now, Kassapa, allow me the sacrificial firehouse.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.12: Having understood that “(permission is) given”, not daunted he entered, unafraid.
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.14: Having seen the Seer enter, the Snake-Dragon, depressed, belched out smoke.
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.16: With intent and gladdened mind the Human-Dragon also belched out smoke right there.
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.18: Unbearably angry, the Snake-Dragon blazed forth like fire.
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.20: Skilled in the fire-element, the Human-Dragon also blazed forth right there,
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.22: They both burned so brightly that the yogis surveying the sacrificial firehouse, (said):
pli-tv-kd1:15.6.25: “The Great Ascetic is surely intelligent, but he is harassed by the Dragon.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.1: With the passing of the night,
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.3: But the multi-coloured flames of the One of Psychic Power remained.
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.5: Then there were blue, red, crimson, yellow, and quartz-coloured
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.7: Multi-coloured flames on the body of Aṅgirasa.
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.9: After putting (him) in his bowl, he showed the Snake-Dragon to the brāhmaṇa, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.11: “This is your Dragon, Kassapa, his psychic power was overcome by (my) power.”
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.13: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa convinced by this psychic miracle of the Fortunate One, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:15.7.14: “Live right here, Great Ascetic, I (will give) a constant supply of food to you.”
pli-tv-kd1:16.1.1: Then the Fortunate One, not far from the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s ashram, dwelt in a certain jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:16.1.2: Then the Four Great Kings, towards the end of the night, having lit up the whole of that jungle thicket with their surpassing beauty, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, they stood at the four directions like a great mass of fire.
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.1: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa, with the passing of that night, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.2: “It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.3: Who were those, Great Ascetic, towards the end of the night, who, having lit up the whole of that jungle thicket with their surpassing beauty, approached you, and after approaching and worshipping you, stood at the four directions like a great mass of fire?”
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.4: “Those, Kassapa, were the Four Great Kings, who approached me to listen to the Dhamma.”
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.5: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.6: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since even the Four Great Kings will approach him to listen to the Dhamma, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.7: Then the Fortunate One, having eaten the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s food, dwelt on in that very jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:16.2.8: The Second Miracle (is Finished) 24. The Third Miracle (Sakka, the Lord of the Gods)
pli-tv-kd1:17.1.1: Then Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, towards the end of the night, having lit up the whole of that jungle thicket with his surpassing beauty, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood at one side like a great mass of fire, (having colours) more brilliant, and more excellent, than the former colours.
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.1: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa, with the passing of that night, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.2: “It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.3: Who was that, Great Ascetic, towards the end of the night, who, having lit up the whole of that jungle thicket with his surpassing beauty, approached you, and after approaching and worshipping you, stood at one side like a great mass of fire, (having colours) more brilliant, and more excellent, than the former colours.”
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.4: “That, Kassapa, was Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, who approached me to listen to the Dhamma.”
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.5: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.6: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since even Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, will approach him to listen to the Dhamma, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:17.2.7: Then the Fortunate One, having eaten the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s food, dwelt on in that very jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:18.1.1: Then Brahmā Sahampati, towards the end of the night, having lit up the whole of that jungle thicket with his surpassing beauty, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he stood at one side like a great mass of fire, (having colours) more brilliant, and more excellent, than the former colours.
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.1: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa, with the passing of that night, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.2: “It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.3: Who was that, Great Ascetic who, towards the end of the night, having lit up the whole of that jungle thicket with his surpassing beauty, approached you, and after approaching and worshipping you, stood at one side like a great mass of fire, (having colours) more brilliant, and more excellent, than the former colours.”
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.4: “That, Kassapa, was Brahmā Sahampati, who approached me to listen to the Dhamma.”
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.5: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.6: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since even Brahmā Sahampati will approach him to listen to the Dhamma, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:18.2.7: Then the Fortunate One, having eaten the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s food, dwelt on in that very jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:19.1.1: Then at that time the yogi Uruvelakassapa had arranged for a great sacrifice, and almost the whole (population) of Aṅga and Magadha, having gathered abundant food and drinks, had a desire to attend.
pli-tv-kd1:19.1.2: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:19.1.3: “Now I have arranged for a great sacrifice, and almost the whole (population) of Aṅga and Magadha, having gathered abundant food and drinks, will attend.
pli-tv-kd1:19.1.4: If the Great Ascetic performs a powerful miracle in the midst of the people his gain and honour will increase, and my gain and honour will decrease.
pli-tv-kd1:19.1.5: Surely the Great Ascetic should not come on the morrow.”
pli-tv-kd1:19.2.1: Then the Fortunate One, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s mind, after approaching Northern Kuru, gathering alms from there, and eating them at lake Anotatta, made his dwelling right there for the day.
pli-tv-kd1:19.2.2: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa, with the passing of that night, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching, he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:19.2.3: “It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.
pli-tv-kd1:19.2.4: Why did you not come yesterday, Great Ascetic?
pli-tv-kd1:19.2.6: ‘Why does the Great Ascetic not come?’
pli-tv-kd1:19.2.7: A portion of the food and drinks was set aside for you.”
pli-tv-kd1:19.3.2: ‘Now I have arranged for a great sacrifice, and almost the whole (population) of Aṅga and Magadha, having gathered abundant food and drinks, will attend. If the Great Ascetic performs a powerful miracle in the midst of the people his gain and honour will increase, and my gain and honour will decrease. Surely the Great Ascetic should not come on the morrow'?
pli-tv-kd1:19.4.1: Then I, Kassapa, knowing with my mind the reflection that had arisen in your mind, after approaching Northern Kuru, gathering alms from there, and eating them at lake Anotatta, made my dwelling right there for the day.”
pli-tv-kd1:19.4.2: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:19.4.3: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since he can even know (my) mind with (his) mind, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:19.4.4: Then the Fortunate One, having eaten the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s food, dwelt on in that very jungle thicket.
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.1: Then at that time there was a rag-robe that had arisen to the Fortunate One.
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.2: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.3: “Now where can I wash this rag-robe?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.4: Then, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the Fortunate One’s mind, having dug a lake with his hand, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.5: “May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, wash the rag-robe here.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.6: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.7: “Now on what can I beat this rag-robe?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.8: Then, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the Fortunate One’s mind, set up a great rock, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:20.1.9: “May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, beat the rag-robe here.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.1: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.2: “Now having grabbed hold of what can I emerge (from the lake)?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.3: Then a god who was living in an Arjuna (tree), knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the Fortunate One’s mind, bent down a branch, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.4: “May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, having grabbed hold here emerge (from the lake).”
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.5: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.6: “Now on what can I stretch out this rag-robe (for drying)?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.7: Then, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the Fortunate One’s mind, set up a great rock, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:20.2.8: “May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, stretch out the rag-robe here.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.3.1: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa, with the passing of that night, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching, he said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.3.2: “It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.
pli-tv-kd1:20.3.3: Now how is it, Great Ascetic, this lake was not here formerly, (and yet) this lake is here?
pli-tv-kd1:20.3.4: This rock was not set up here formerly:
pli-tv-kd1:20.3.5: this rock was set up by whom?
pli-tv-kd1:20.3.6: This branch of the Arjuna (tree) was not bent down formerly, (and yet) this branch is bent down (now)?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.1: “Here, Kassapa, a rag-robe arose to me.
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.2: Then, Kassapa, this occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.3: ‘Now where can I wash this rag-robe?’
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.4: Then, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, Kassapa, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in my mind, having dug a lake with his hand, said this to me:
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.5: ‘May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, wash the rag-robe here,’
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.6: the lake was dug by the divine being himself with his own hand.
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.7: Then this, Kassapa, occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.8: ‘Now on what can I beat this rag-robe?’
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.9: Then, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, Kassapa, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in my mind, set up a great rock, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.10: ‘May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, beat the rag-robe here,’
pli-tv-kd1:20.4.11: the rock was set up by the divine being himself.
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.1: Then, Kassapa, this occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.2: ‘Now having grabbed hold of what can I emerge (from the lake)?’
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.3: Then, Kassapa, a god who was living in an Arjuna (tree), knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in my mind, bent down a branch, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.4: ‘May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, having grabbed hold here emerge (from the lake),’
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.5: this Arjuna (tree-spirit) gave a hand himself.
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.6: Then, Kassapa, this occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.7: ‘Now on what can I stretch out this rag-robe (for drying)?’
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.8: Then, Kassapa, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in my mind, set up a great rock, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.9: ‘May the Fortunate One, venerable Sir, stretch out the rag-robe here,’
pli-tv-kd1:20.5.10: the rock was set up by this divine being himself.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.6.1: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.6.2: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since even Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, does (him) service, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.6.3: Then the Fortunate One, having eaten the yogi Uruvelakassapa’s food, dwelt on in that very jungle thicket.

pli-tv-kd1:20.7.2: “It is time, Great Ascetic, the meal is ready.”

pli-tv-kd1:20.8.2: “By what path, Great Ascetic, did you come,

pli-tv-kd1:20.9.1: “Here, Kassapa, after sending you away, picking a fruit from the Rose-Apple (tree), (after which) the Rose-Apple Island is named, and arriving earlier, I sat down in the sacrificial firehouse.

pli-tv-kd1:20.12.1: Then at that time those yogis who wanted to tend the sacred fires were not able to chop the firewood.
pli-tv-kd1:20.12.2: Then this occurred to those yogis:
pli-tv-kd1:20.12.3: “No doubt it is because of the Great Ascetic’s psychic power that we are not able to chop the firewood.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.12.4: Then the Fortunate One said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.12.7: and more than five hundred pieces of firewood were chopped.
pli-tv-kd1:20.12.8: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.12.9: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since (on his say so) firewood can be chopped, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.1: Then at that time those yogis who wanted to tend the sacred fires were not able to light the fires.
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.2: Then this occurred to those yogis:
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.3: “No doubt it is because of the Great Ascetic’s psychic power that we are not able to light the sacred fires.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.4: Then the Fortunate One said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.5: “Let the sacred fires be lit, Kassapa.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.7: and more than five hundred sacred fires were lit.
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.8: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.13.9: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since (on his say so) sacred fires can be lit, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.1: Then at that time those yogis, after tending the sacred fires, were not able to put the sacred fires out.
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.2: Then this occurred to those yogis:
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.3: “No doubt it is because of the Great Ascetic’s psychic power that we are not able to put out the sacred fires.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.4: Then the Fortunate One said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.5: “Let the sacred fires be put out, Kassapa.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.6: “Let them be put out, Great Ascetic,”
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.7: and more than five hundred sacred fires were put out.
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.8: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.14.9: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since (on his say so) sacred fires can be put out, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.15.1: Then at that time those yogis, in the cold Winter nights, in between ‘the eights’, at the time of the snowfall, in the river Nerañjarā, were plunging in, and plunging out, were plunging in and out.
pli-tv-kd1:20.15.2: Then the Fortunate One created about five hundred coal-pans, where those yogis, after emerging, warmed (themselves).
pli-tv-kd1:20.15.3: Then this occurred to those yogis:
pli-tv-kd1:20.15.4: “No doubt it is because of the Great Ascetic’s psychic power that these coal-pans were created.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.15.5: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.15.6: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since he can create so many coal-pans for them, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.1: Then at that time a great cloud poured down out of season, and a great flood-water arose,
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.2: and in that area where the Fortunate One was living the (whole) place became submerged with water.
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.3: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.4: “Now what if I, having risen above the water on all sides, were to walk (on an island) in the middle on dusty ground?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.5: Then the Fortunate One, having risen above the water on all sides, walked (on an island) in the middle of dusty ground.
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.7: ‘May the Great Ascetic not be carried away by water.’ with a boat and a great many yogis went to that place in the area where the Fortunate One was living.
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.8: The yogi Uruvelakassapa saw that the Fortunate One, having risen above the water on all sides, was walking (on an island) in the middle of dusty ground,
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.11: and after rising up into the sky, he reappeared in the boat.
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.12: Then this occurred to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.16.13: “Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, since even the water cannot carry him away, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.1: Then this occurred to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.2: “For a long time this will occur to that foolish fellow:
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.3: ‘Powerful and majestic is this Great Ascetic, but he is surely not a Worthy One like I am.’
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.4: Now what if I were to cause spiritual anxiety to this yogi?”
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.5: Then the Fortunate One said this to the yogi Uruvelakassapa:
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.6: “You are certainly not a Worthy One, Kassapa. Nor have you entered the path to Worthiness.
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.7: This practice of yours is not one whereby you could be a Worthy One, or one who has entered the path to Worthiness.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.8: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa, having fallen with his head at the Fortunate One’s feet, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.17.9: “May I receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may I receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.18.1: “But you Kassapa, are the leader, guide, chief, director and instructor of five hundred yogis,
pli-tv-kd1:20.18.2: you should them give permission and they can do whatever they are thinking.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.18.3: Then the yogi Uruvelakassapa approached those yogis, and after approaching he said this to those yogis:
pli-tv-kd1:20.18.4: “I wish to live the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic, you, dear friends, can do whatever you are thinking.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.18.5: [They replied:] “For a long time, friend, we have had confidence in the Great Ascetic, if you, friend, will live the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic, all of us will live the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.19.1: Then those yogis, after throwing their hair, locks, pole and basket and sacred fire equipment into the water, approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and falling with their heads at the feet of the Fortunate One, they said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:20.19.2: “May we receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may we receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.19.3: “Come, monks,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:20.19.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:20.19.5: That was these venerable ones’ full ordination.

pli-tv-kd1:20.20.2: “Let there be no danger for my brothers,”

pli-tv-kd1:20.24.1: Through the Fortunate One’s determining five hundred pieces of firewood that were not chopped were chopped,
pli-tv-kd1:20.24.2: fires that were not lit were lit,
pli-tv-kd1:20.24.3: that were not put out were put out,
pli-tv-kd1:20.24.5: In this way there were three and a half thousand miracles.
pli-tv-kd1:21.1.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dwelt at Uruvelā for as long as he liked, left on walking tour for Gayā’s Head, together with a great Community of monks, with a thousand monks all of whom were formerly yogis.
pli-tv-kd1:21.1.2: There the Fortunate One dwelt near Gayā, on Gayā’s Head together with a thousand monks.
pli-tv-kd1:21.2.1: There the Fortunate One addressed the monks, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:21.2.3: What all is burning, monks? The eye is burning, monks, forms are burning,
pli-tv-kd1:21.2.4: eye-consciousness is burning, eye-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on eye-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, that also is burning.
pli-tv-kd1:21.2.6: It is burning with the fire of passion, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, with old age and death, with griefs, with lamentations, with pains, with sorrows, and with despairs, I say.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.1: The ear is burning, sounds are burning, ear-consciousness is burning, ear-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on ear-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, that also is burning.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.3: It is burning with the fire of passion, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, with old age and death, with griefs, with lamentations, with pains, with sorrows, and with despairs, I say.

pli-tv-kd1:21.3.7: The tongue is burning, tastes are burning, tongue-consciousness is burning, tongue-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on tongue-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, that also is burning.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.9: It is burning with the fire of passion, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, with old age and death, with griefs, with lamentations, with pains, with sorrows, and with despairs, I say.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.10: The body is burning, tangibles are burning, body-consciousness is burning, body-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on body-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, that also is burning.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.12: It is burning with the fire of passion, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, with old age and death, with griefs, with lamentations, with pains, with sorrows, and with despairs, I say.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.13: The mind is burning, thoughts are burning, mind-consciousness is burning, mind-contact is burning, and whatever feeling arises dependent on mind-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, that also is burning.
pli-tv-kd1:21.3.15: It is burning with the fire of passion, with the fire of hatred, with the fire of delusion. It is burning with birth, with old age and death, with griefs, with lamentations, with pains, with sorrows, and with despairs, I say.
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.1: Seeing this, monks, the learned Noble disciple grows weary of the eye, grows weary of forms, grows weary of eye-consciousness, grows weary of eye-contact, and whatever feeling that arises dependent on eye-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, he also grows weary of that.
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.2: He grows weary of the ear, grows weary of sounds, grows weary of ear-consciousness, grows weary of ear-contact, and whatever feeling that arises dependent on ear-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, he also grows weary of that.
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.3: He grows weary of the nose, grows weary of scents, grows weary of nose-consciousness, grows weary of nose-contact, and whatever feeling that arises dependent on nose-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, he also grows weary of that.
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.4: He grows weary of the tongue, grows weary of tastes, grows weary of tongue-consciousness, grows weary of tongue-contact, and whatever feeling that arises dependent on tongue-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, he also grows weary of that.
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.5: He grows weary of the body, grows weary of tangibles,
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.6: grows weary of body-consciousness, grows weary of body-contact, and whatever feeling that arises dependent on body-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, he also grows weary of that. He grows weary of the mind, grows weary of thoughts, grows weary of mind-consciousness, grows weary of mind-contact, and whatever feeling that arises dependent on mind-contact, whether pleasant, unpleasant, or neither-unpleasant-nor-pleasant, he also grows weary of that,
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.7: through weariness he becomes dispassionate, through dispassion he is liberated, in liberation, there is the knowledge that such is liberation:
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.8: ‘Destroyed is (re)birth accomplished is the spiritual life done is what ought to be done there is no more of this mundane state - this he knows.’
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.9: Moreover, as this sermon was being given, those one thousand monks’ minds were liberated from the pollutants, without attachment.
pli-tv-kd1:21.4.10: The Instruction about Burning is Finished
pli-tv-kd1:22.1.1: Then the Fortunate One, having dwelt at Gayā’s Head for as long as he liked, left on walking tour for Rājagaha, together with a great Community of monks, with a thousand monks all of whom were formerly yogis.
pli-tv-kd1:22.1.2: Then the Fortunate One, walking gradually on walking tour, went and entered Rājagaha.
pli-tv-kd1:22.1.3: There the Fortunate One dwelt near Rājagaha, by the Suppatiṭṭha Shrine in the Palmyra Wood.
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.1: The Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra heard:
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.2: “The ascetic Gotama, the Sakyan Son, who has gone forth from the Sakya family, has arrived in Rājagaha, and is dwelling near Rājagaha, by the Suppatiṭṭha Shrine in the Palmyra Garden.
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.3: But about that Fortunate One Gotama this beautiful report has gone round:
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.4: ‘Such is he, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha, the one endowed with understanding and good conduct, the Happy One, the one who understands the worlds, the unsurpassed guide for those people who need taming, the Teacher of gods and men, the Buddha, the Fortunate One.’
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.5: This world with its gods, Māra, and Brahmā, this generation, with its ascetics and brāhmaṇas, princes and men, he makes known, after gaining deep knowledge for himself.
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.6: He teaches the Dhamma (which is) good in the beginning, good in the middle, good in the end; with its meaning, with its (proper) phrasing; and explains the spiritual life which is complete, full and pure.
pli-tv-kd1:22.2.7: But the sight of such Worthy Ones is good.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.3.1: Then the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra, surrounded by twelve myriads of brāhmaṇas and householders from Magadha approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and worshipping the Fortunate One, he sat down at one side. Of those twelve myriads of brāhmaṇas and householders from Magadha, some, after worshipping the Fortunate One, sat down on one side. Some exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:22.3.2: Some, after raising their hands in respectful salutation to the Fortunate One, sat down on one side. Some, after announcing their name and family to the Fortunate One, sat down on one side. Some, while keeping silent, sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.1: Then this occurred to those twelve myriads of brāhmaṇas and householders from Magadha:
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.2: “How is it: does the Great Ascetic live the spiritual life under Uruvelakassapa, or does Uruvelakassapa live the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic?”
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.3: Then the Fortunate One, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the minds of the Magadhan brāhmaṇas and householders, addressed the venerable Uruvelakassapa with a verse:
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.4: “ Having seen what did you, one of Uruvelā,
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.5: Who spoke of austerity, give up the sacrificial fire?
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.6: I ask you the reason for this, Kassapa,
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.7: Why did you give up the fire sacrifice?”
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.8: “ The sacrifices speak of forms, sounds,
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.9: And also tastes, sensuality, and women.
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.10: Having understood that in the attachments ‘this is a stain’,
pli-tv-kd1:22.4.11: I therefore take no delight in offerings and sacrifices.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.5.1: “If your mind takes no delight, Kassapa,” said the Fortunate One,
pli-tv-kd1:22.5.4: Then where in the world with its gods and men,
pli-tv-kd1:22.5.5: Does your mind take delight, Kassapa, speak about this.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.5.6: “Having seen the state of peace, free of attachments,
pli-tv-kd1:22.5.7: (That) nothingness, unattached to the sensual realm,
pli-tv-kd1:22.5.9: I therefore take no delight in offerings and sacrifices.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.6.1: Then the venerable Uruvelakassapa, after rising from his seat, arranging his outer robe on one shoulder, and falling with his head at the feet of the Fortunate One, said to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:22.6.2: “The Fortunate One is my Teacher, venerable Sir, I am his disciple,
pli-tv-kd1:22.6.3: the Fortunate One is my Teacher, venerable Sir, I am his disciple.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.6.4: Then this occurred to those twelve myriads of brāhmaṇas and householders from Magadha:
pli-tv-kd1:22.6.5: “Uruvelakassapa lives the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.7.1: Then the Fortunate One, knowing with his mind the reflection that had arisen in the minds of the Magadhan brāhmaṇas and householders, spoke about the gradual teaching to them, that is to say: talk about giving, talk about virtue, talk about heaven,
pli-tv-kd1:22.7.2: the danger, degradation, and defilement of sensual desires, and the advantages of renunciation, (these) he explained.
pli-tv-kd1:22.7.3: When the Fortunate One knew that they had ready minds, pliable minds, open minds, uplifted minds, confident minds, he explained to them the Dhamma teaching the Awakened Ones have discovered themselves:
pli-tv-kd1:22.8.1: Just as it is known that a clean cloth without a stain will take the dye well,
pli-tv-kd1:22.8.2: just so to eleven myriads of the Magadhan brāhmaṇas and householders, with Bimbisāra at their head on that very seat, the dust-free, stainless Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:22.8.3: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.8.4: and one myriad (of them) made known their state as lay-followers.
pli-tv-kd1:22.9.1: Then the Māgadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra, having seen the Dhamma, attained the Dhamma, understood the Dhamma, penetrated the Dhamma, crossed over uncertainty, being without doubts, having attained full confidence, having become independent of others in the Teacher’s teaching, said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:22.9.2: “Formerly, venerable Sir, when I was a boy I had five wishes which are fulfilled for me now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.9.3: Formerly, venerable Sir, when I was a boy this occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:22.9.4: ‘Oh, may I be anointed (King) in the Kingdom’ - this was my first wish, venerable Sir, which has been fulfilled for me now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.9.5: ‘May a Worthy One, a Perfect Sambuddha enter into my realm’ - this was my second wish, venerable Sir, which has been fulfilled for me now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.10.1: ‘May I attend on that Fortunate One’ - this was my third wish, venerable Sir, which has been fulfilled for me now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.10.2: ‘May that Fortunate One teach me the Dhamma’ - this was my fourth wish, venerable Sir, which has been fulfilled for me now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.10.3: ‘May I understand that Fortunate One’s Dhamma' - this was my fifth wish, venerable Sir, which has been fulfilled for me now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.10.4: Formerly, venerable Sir, when I was a boy I had these five wishes and these I am successful in now.
pli-tv-kd1:22.11.1: Excellent, venerable Sir! Excellent, venerable Sir!
pli-tv-kd1:22.11.2: Just as, venerable Sir, one might set upright what has been overturned, or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost, or carry an oil lamp into the darkness, (thinking): ‘those with vision will see forms’,
pli-tv-kd1:22.11.3: just so has the Dhamma been explained by the Fortunate One in countless ways.
pli-tv-kd1:22.11.4: I go, venerable Sir, to the Fortunate One for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Community of monks.
pli-tv-kd1:22.11.5: Please bear it in mind, Fortunate One, that I am a lay follower who has gone for refuge from today forward for as long as I have the breath of life. May the Fortunate One consent, reverend Sir, to me (offering him) a meal on the morrow, together with the Community of monks.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.11.6: The Fortunate One consented by maintaining silence.
pli-tv-kd1:22.12.1: Then the Māgadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra, having understood the Fortunate One’s consent, after rising from his seat, worshipping and circumambulating the Fortunate One, went away.
pli-tv-kd1:22.12.2: Then the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra, with the passing of that night, having had excellent food and drinks made ready,
pli-tv-kd1:22.12.3: had the time announced to the Fortunate One, (saying): “It is time, reverend Sir, the meal is ready.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.12.4: Then the Fortunate One, having dressed in the morning time, after taking up his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha, together with a great Community of monks, with a thousand monks all of whom were formerly yogis.
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.1: Then at that time Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, having created (for himself) the form of a young brāhmaṇa, went ahead of the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head singing these verses:
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.2: The Tamed One with the Tamed, with the former yogis, the Liberated One with the Liberated,
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.4: The Fortunate One who has skin like a golden coin has entered Rājagaha.
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.6: The Freed One with the Freed, with the former yogis, the Liberated One with the Liberated,
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.8: The Fortunate One who has skin like a golden coin has entered Rājagaha.
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.10: The One Gone Beyond with those Gone Beyond, with the former yogis, the Liberated One with the Liberated,
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.12: The Fortunate One who has skin like a golden coin has entered Rājagaha.
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.14: The Peaceful One with the Peaceful, with the former yogis, the Liberated One with the Liberated,
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.16: The Fortunate One who has skin like a golden coin has entered Rājagaha.
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.18: The One of Ten Abidings, Ten Strengths, knowing the Ten Things, endowed with Ten,
pli-tv-kd1:22.13.20: The Fortunate One surrounded by the ten-hundred has entered Rājagaha.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.14.1: This occurred to the people, after seeing Sakka, the Lord of the Gods:
pli-tv-kd1:22.14.2: “Handsome, indeed is this young brāhmaṇa, beautiful, indeed is this young brāhmaṇa, pleasing, indeed is this young brāhmaṇa,
pli-tv-kd1:22.14.3: now just who is this young brāhmaṇa?”
pli-tv-kd1:22.14.4: After this was said, Sakka, the Lord of the Gods, addressed those people with a verse:
pli-tv-kd1:22.14.5: “He who is firm, tamed in every way, pure, a person unmatched,
pli-tv-kd1:22.14.7: A Worthy One, a Happy One - I am his attendant in the world.”
pli-tv-kd1:22.15.1: Then the Fortunate One approached the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra’s residence, and after approaching he sat down on the prepared seat, together with the Community of monks.
pli-tv-kd1:22.15.2: Then the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra, after serving and satisfying with his own hand the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head with excellent food and drinks, when the Fortunate One had eaten and washed his hand and bowl, sat down on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:22.16.1: While sittting on one side this occurred to the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra:
pli-tv-kd1:22.16.2: “Now where can the Fortunate One dwell
pli-tv-kd1:22.16.3: that is neither too far from a village nor too near, easy for coming and going, approachable for people who desire (to hear the Dhamma), uncrowded during the day, with little sound at night, little noise, which has a lonely atmosphere, lying hidden away from men, which is suitable for seclusion?”
pli-tv-kd1:22.17.1: Then this occurred to the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra:
pli-tv-kd1:22.17.2: “This Bamboo Wood garden of ours is neither too far from the village nor too near, easy for coming and going, approachable for people who desire (to hear the Dhamma), uncrowded during the day, with little sound at night, little noise, which has a lonely atmosphere, lying hidden away from men, which is suitable for seclusion.
pli-tv-kd1:22.17.3: Now what if I were to give the Bamboo Wood garden to the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head?”
pli-tv-kd1:22.18.1: Then the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra having taken a golden water vessel, dedicated (it) to the Fortunate One, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:22.18.2: “Can I give this Bamboo Wood garden, venerable Sir, to the Community of monks with the Buddha at its head?”
pli-tv-kd1:22.18.3: The Fortunate One accepted the park.
pli-tv-kd1:22.18.4: Then the Fortunate One, after instructing, rousing, enthusing, and cheering the Magadhan King Seniya Bimbisāra with a Dhamma talk, having risen from his seat, went away.
pli-tv-kd1:22.18.5: Then the Fortunate One, with this as the basis, after giving a Dhamma talk, addressed the monks, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:23.1.0: 41. The Story of the Going-Forth of Sāriputta and Moggallāna
pli-tv-kd1:23.1.1: Then at that time the wanderer Sañjaya was living near Rājagaha together with a great assembly of wanderers, with two hundred and fifty wanderers.
pli-tv-kd1:23.1.2: Then at that time Sāriputta and Moggallāna were living the spiritual life under the wanderer Sañjaya,
pli-tv-kd1:23.1.3: and there was an agreement amongst themselves:
pli-tv-kd1:23.1.4: “Whoever attains the Deathless first, he should inform the other.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.2.1: Then the venerable Assaji, having dressed in the morning time, after taking up his bowl and robe, entered Rājagaha for alms, pleasing in going forwards, in going back, in looking ahead, in looking around, in bending, in stretching, having downcast eyes, and endowed with good posture. The wanderer Sāriputta saw the venerable Assaji walking for alms in Rājagaha, pleasing in going forwards, in going back, in looking ahead, in looking around,
pli-tv-kd1:23.2.2: in bending, in stretching, having downcast eyes, and endowed with good posture,
pli-tv-kd1:23.2.3: and having seen (him), this occurred to him:
pli-tv-kd1:23.2.4: “Of those in the world who are Worthy or have entered the path to Worthiness this monk is a certain one of them.
pli-tv-kd1:23.2.5: Now what if I, having approached this monk, were to ask:
pli-tv-kd1:23.2.6: ‘On account of whom, friend, did you go forth, who is your teacher, what Dhamma do you prefer?’”
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.1: Then this occurred to the wanderer Sāriputta:
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.2: “This is the wrong time to ask the monk, he has entered amongst the houses for alms.
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.3: Now what if I were to follow along closely behind this monk with a desire (to find) the path he has found?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.4: Then the venerable Assaji, after walking for alms in Rājagaha and taking his alms food, went back.
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.5: Then the wanderer Sāriputta approached the venerable Assaji, and after approaching he exchanged greetings with the venerable Assaji, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, he stood on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.6: While standing on one side the wanderer Sāriputta said this to the venerable Assaji:
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.7: “Your faculties, friend, are very clear, purified is your skin and bright,
pli-tv-kd1:23.3.8: on account of whom, friend, did you go forth, who is your teacher, what Dhamma do you prefer?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.1: “There is, friend, a Great Ascetic, a Sakyan Son, who has gone forth from the Sakya family, on account of that Fortunate One I went forth, that Fortunate One is my Teacher, that Fortunate One’s Dhamma I prefer.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.2: “But what is the doctrine of the venerable’s Teacher, what does he say?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.3: “I am new, friend, one not long gone forth, recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline, I am not able to teach the Dhamma at length, but I can explain the meaning to you in brief.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.4: Then the wanderer Sāriputta said this to the venerable Assaji:
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.6: Speak little or much, but tell the meaning to me,
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.8: The meaning is useful to me,
pli-tv-kd1:23.4.9: what to do with many words?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.1: Then the venerable Assaji recited this Dhamma instruction to the wanderer Sāriputta:
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.2: “Whatever things have a cause and source, their cause the Realised One has told,
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.4: And also that which is their cessation - such is the Great Ascetic’s doctrine.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.6: Then to the wanderer Sāriputta, after hearing this Dhamma instruction, the dust-free, stainless Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.7: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.8: And he said: “This really is the Dhamma if you have penetrated the Sorrowless State,
pli-tv-kd1:23.5.10: unseen through many myriads of past aeons.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.6.1: Then the wanderer Sāriputta approached the wanderer Moggallāna.
pli-tv-kd1:23.6.2: The wanderer Moggallāna saw the wanderer Sāriputta coming while still far away, and after seeing (him), he said this to the wanderer Sāriputta:
pli-tv-kd1:23.6.3: “Your faculties, friend, are very clear, purified is your skin and bright,
pli-tv-kd1:23.6.4: have you, friend, attained the Deathless?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.6.5: “Yes, friend, I have attained the Deathless.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.6.6: “But how did you, friend, attain the Deathless?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.7.1: “Here, friend, I saw the monk Assaji walking for alms in Rājagaha, pleasing in going forwards, in going back, in looking ahead, in looking around, in bending, in stretching, having downcast eyes, and endowed with good posture,
pli-tv-kd1:23.7.2: and having seen (him), this occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:23.7.3: ‘Of those in the world who are Worthy or have entered the path to Worthiness this monk is one of them.’
pli-tv-kd1:23.7.4: Now what if I, having approached this monk, were to ask:
pli-tv-kd1:23.7.5: “On account of whom, friend, did you go forth, who is your teacher, what Dhamma do you prefer?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.8.1: Then this, friend, occurred to me:
pli-tv-kd1:23.8.2: “This is the wrong time to ask the monk, he has entered amongst the houses for alms. Now what if I were to follow along close behind this monk with a desire to find out the path?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.8.3: Then, friend, the monk Assaji, after walking for alms in Rājagaha, and taking his alms food, went back.
pli-tv-kd1:23.8.4: Then I, friend, approached the monk Assaji, and after approaching I exchanged greetings with the monk Assaji, and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, I stood on one side.
pli-tv-kd1:23.8.5: While standing on one side, friend, I said this to the monk Assaji:
pli-tv-kd1:23.8.6: “Your faculties, friend, are very clear, purified is your skin and bright,
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.1: on account of whom, friend, did you go forth, who is your teacher, what Dhamma do you prefer?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.2: “There is, friend, a Great Ascetic, the Sakyan Son, who has gone forth from the Sakya family, on account of that Fortunate One I went forth, that Fortunate One is my Teacher, that Fortunate One’s Dhamma I prefer.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.3: “But what is the doctrine of the venerable’s Teacher, what does he say?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.4: “I am new, friend, not long gone forth, recently come to this Dhamma and Discipline, I am not able to teach the Dhamma at length, but I can explain the meaning to you in brief.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.5: Then, friend, I said this to the venerable Assaji: “Friend,
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.7: Speak little or much, but tell the meaning to me,
pli-tv-kd1:23.9.9: The meaning is useful to me, what to do with many words?”
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.1: Then, friend, the monk Assaji recited this Dhamma instruction:
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.2: “Whatever things have a cause and source, their cause the Realised One told,
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.4: And also that which is their cessation - such is the Great Ascetic’s doctrine.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.6: Then to the wanderer Moggallāna, after hearing this Dhamma instruction, the dust-free, stainless Vision-of-the-Dhamma arose:
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.7: “Whatever has the nature of arising, all that has the nature of ceasing.”
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.8: And he said: “This really is the Dhamma if you have penetrated the Sorrowless State,
pli-tv-kd1:23.10.10: unseen through many myriads of past aeons.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.1: Then the wanderer Moggallāna said this to the wanderer Sāriputta:
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.2: “Let us go, friend, to the Fortunate One, the Fortunate One is the Teacher for us.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.3: “These two hundred and fifty wanderers, friend, are living here depending on us, looking to us,
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.4: we should get their permission, then whatever they will think that they will do.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.5: Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached those wanderers, and after approaching, they said this to those wanderers:
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.6: “We are going, friends, to the Fortunate One, the Fortunate One is the Teacher for us.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.1.7: “We are living here depending on you, venerable ones, looking to you, venerable ones, if you venerable ones will live the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic all of us will surely live the spiritual life under the Great Ascetic.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.1: Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached the wanderer Sañjaya, and after approaching, they said this to the wanderer Sañjaya:
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.2: “We are going, friend, to the Fortunate One, the Fortunate One is our Teacher.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.3: “Enough, friend, don't go, the three of us will look after this group.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.4: For a second time Sāriputta and Moggallāna said this to the wanderer Sañjaya: “We are going, friend, to the Fortunate One, the Fortunate One is our Teacher.” “Enough, friend, don't go, the three of us will look after this group.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.5: For a third time Sāriputta and Moggallāna said this to the wanderer Sañjaya:
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.6: “We are going, friend, to the Fortunate One, the Fortunate One is our Teacher.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.2.7: “Enough, friend, don't go, the three of us will look after this group.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.1: Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna taking those two hundred and fifty wanderers approached the Bamboo Wood.
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.2: But the wanderer Sañjaya right there threw up hot blood from his mouth.
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.3: The Fortunate One saw Sāriputta and Moggallāna coming while still far away, and having seen (them), he addressed the monks, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.4: “These two companions who are coming, Kolita and Upatissa,
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.5: will be my pair of Chief Disciples, an auspicious pair.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.6: After (they had) attained deep knowledge in the realm of unsurpassed liberation with the destruction of attachments
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.8: The Teacher then spoke about them in the Bamboo Wood, (saying):
pli-tv-kd1:24.3.12: Will be my pair of Chief Disciples, an auspicious pair.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.4.1: Then Sāriputta and Moggallāna approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching and falling with their heads at the feet of the Fortunate One, they said this to the Fortunate One:
pli-tv-kd1:24.4.2: “May we receive the going-forth, venerable Sir, in the presence of the Fortunate One, may we receive the full ordination.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.4.3: “Come, monks,” said the Fortunate One, “the Dhamma has been well-proclaimed,
pli-tv-kd1:24.4.4: live the spiritual life for the complete ending of suffering.”
pli-tv-kd1:24.4.5: That was these venerable ones’ full ordination.
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.0: 42. The Going-Forth of the Well-Known (Sons of Good Families)
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.1: Then at that time many well-known sons of good families from Magadha were living the spiritual life under the Fortunate One.
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.3: “The Ascetic Gotama’s method is making (families) childless, the Ascetic Gotama’s method is causing breakage and loss, the Ascetic Gotama’s method is family-smashing, now through him a thousand yogis have gone forth, and these two-hundred and fifty of Sañjaya’s wanderers have gone forth,
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.4: and these many well-known sons of good families from Magadha are (all) living the spiritual life under the Ascetic Gotama,”
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.5: and having seen the monks, they scolded them with this verse:
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.6: “The Great Ascetic has come to Giribbaja in Magadha
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.8: After leading off all those under Sañjaya,
pli-tv-kd1:24.5.9: who will he lead off now?”
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.1: The monks heard those people grumbling, moaning, cursing.
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.2: Then those monks informed the Fortunate One of it.
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.3: “This noise will not last long, monks, it will last for only seven days, and with the passing of seven days it will disappear.
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.4: Therefore, monks, whoever scolds you with this verse:
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.5: ‘The Great Ascetic has come to Giribbaja in Magadha
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.7: After leading off all those under Sañjaya,
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.8: who will he lead off now?’
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.9: you scold them back with this verse:
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.10: ‘The Great Heros, the Realised Ones, lead with the True Dhamma,
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.12: By the Dhamma they are leading,
pli-tv-kd1:24.6.13: why be jealous of the wise?’”
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.1: Then at that time people, after seeing the monks, scolded them with this verse:
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.2: “The Great Ascetic has come to Giribbaja in Magadha
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.4: After leading off all those under Sañjaya,
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.5: who will he lead off now?”
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.6: and the monks scolded those people back with this verse:
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.7: “The Great Heros, the Realised Ones, lead with the True Dhamma,
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.9: By the Dhamma they are leading,
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.10: why be jealous of the wise?”
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.11: “It seems the people and ascetics (are led) with Dhamma by the Sakyan son, they are not led by what is not Dhamma.” That noise lasted only seven days, and with the passing of those seven days it disappeared.
pli-tv-kd1:24.7.12: The Going Forth of Sāriputta and Moggallāna is Finished
